content:
- **Outage**: 14 Mar, 09:12‑09:55 UTC – Brightloom checkout API returned 503 for all payment‑confirmation requests, affecting ~18,400 customers and ~2,150 abandoned orders.  
- **Trigger**: A staging‑only config change lowered `max_client_conn` from 2000 to 200 in production, causing pool saturation.  
- **Detection & Response**: Error rate spiked at 09:12; status page updated within 6 min; rollback completed in <3 min, restoring baseline by 10:02.  
- **Root Cause**: Merge conflict removed the `env: staging` guard in a single‑YAML config, so the staging value applied to production without review.  
- **Action Items**: CI check for env keys, alert on >80% pool saturation, and refund ~6,300 EUR in processing fees.

- **New features**: Parallel uploads (up to 8 files, default 4), resumable pushes via `--resume`, and a `tidewater doctor` command for credential/proxy/clock checks.  
- **Performance**: Upload time for a 1.2 GB folder dropped from 14 min to 5 min with parallel uploads.  
- **Breaking changes**: `--legacy-auth` flag removed; token files in `~/.tidewater/token` require a new `tidewater login`. `tidewater list` now outputs JSON by default when stdout is not a terminal.  
- **Bug fixes**: Windows crash with trailing‑dot paths, incorrect exit code on checksum mismatch, and corrected `--dry-run` help text.  
- **Other updates**: Documentation moved to `docs.example.com`; Homebrew formula updated; Docker image now uses Alpine 3.19; 14 community contributors thanked.

- Mobile onboarding now 61 % complete (up from 48 %); 30 % drop at notifications screen, plan to move prompt after first saved item (Android 3.7.2, iOS 3.8).  
- Pricing page A/B test: Variant B (annual‑first layout) converted at 4.1 % vs 3.4 % control; 22,000 visitors per arm; roll out B with 10 % holdback for two weeks.  
- Office move: new space opens 15 January; no immediate action required.  
- Design team coffee tasting scheduled Thursday; unrelated to other items.

- Draft RFC‑0042 proposes using an `Idempotency-Key` header (UUIDv4) for `POST /orders` to prevent duplicate orders caused by retries.  
- The server stores the key, a hash of the request body, and the final response for 24 h; it returns the stored response with `Idempotent-Replay: true` if the same key and body hash are received again.  
- If the same key is reused with a different body hash, the server replies `422 Unprocessable Entity` with error code `idempotency_key_reuse`; if the original request is still processing, it replies `409 Conflict` and advises retry after the `Retry-After` interval.  
- Idempotency keys are scoped per API credential, avoiding collisions between customers, and records are kept in Redis under the `idem:` prefix (≈2 KB each, ~40 GB peak).  
- Alternatives such as auto‑deriving keys, mandatory headers, or PostgreSQL storage were rejected; open questions remain about configurable TTLs and whether `PATCH` requests should be covered.

- Sprinting is powerful but should not dominate movement; current prototype shows 78 % sprint usage, which is too high.  
- Stamina caps at 100 at level 1, increases 5 per level up to 150; sprint drains 12 stamina/s, regen 8 stamina/s after 1.5 s delay.  
- When stamina reaches 0 the player becomes “winded”: speed drops to 60 % for 3 s, sprint locked until stamina ≥ 25.  
- Sprinting is disabled when carrying a heavy object or swimming deeper than knee height; dodge rolls cost 20 stamina and ignore winded state.  
- Playtests aim for 30–40 % sprint usage; a full sprint from 100 stamina lasts ~8.3 s, covering ~62 m at 7.5 m/s.

- Export failure halted Harlow & Finch Ltd’s month‑end reporting, risking a missed deadline.  
- A temporary timeout increase allowed the full 410,000‑record export to complete, restoring data availability.  
- A permanent fix is scheduled for 6 Feb, and a €10 account credit was issued as compensation.

- Q3 revenue reached **$18.6 M** (↑ 11% vs Q2, ↑ 24% YoY), with **$15.9 M** from subscriptions and **$2.7 M** from professional services (flat).  
- **1,284** paying accounts, net +73; churn 2.3%; enterprise accounts grew from 41 to 47.  
- Gross margin improved to **74%** (from 71%) due to an 8% drop in cloud hosting costs; operating margin was **‑6%** (vs ‑9% Q2).  
- Q4 qualified pipeline is **$31 M** with a 22% win rate; EMEA contributes 38% of new pipeline.  
- Headcount at **412** (↑ 19 from Q2); engineering +11 hires, sales +5; Lisbon off‑site cost $140 k under G&A.

- A 21‑day pilot with 96 undergraduates tested whether a daily text reminder to start winding down 45 min before bedtime improved morning attention, measured by a 5‑minute psychomotor vigilance task (PVT).  
- The reminder group reduced PVT lapses from 7.9 to 5.6 (difference‑in‑differences –1.8 lapses, 95 % CI –3.4 to –0.2) and increased self‑reported time in bed by 22 min, while the control group showed minimal change.  
- Limitations include a convenience sample of psychology students, no placebo message for controls, a non‑exam period, and a small actigraphy subgroup; a larger preregistered trial is planned.

- Monthly Managed Plus fees rise 6.5 % (with a 24‑month renewal before 15 Dec keeping the old price until 30 Jun).  
- Uptime commitment increases to 99.95 %; service credits now 10 % of the fee per 0.1 % shortfall, capped at 50 % (previously 30 %).  
- Backup retention extends to 35 days; longer retention can be added at 0.02 EUR/GB/month.  
- Termination notice without cause extends from 60 to 90 days; breach termination remains 30‑day cure period.  
- Phone support shifts to 07:00‑21:00 CET weekdays; 24/7 ticketing and emergency line stay unchanged.

- **Day 1 onboarding**: laptop shipped, buddy walkthrough at 10 AM, manager goal‑setting at 2 PM; do not install tools until IT enables the account.  
- **Accounts & access**: GitHub, cloud console, on‑call tool within 48 h; production access requires 90‑min security training; VPN mandatory off‑site.  
- **Week 1 tasks**: read the architecture overview, submit a “first PR” (documentation or log fix) by Friday, attend the 4 PM engineering demo.  
- **Week 2 tasks**: shadow an on‑call shift with the buddy, pick a `good-first-issue` ticket from the board.  
- **Practicalities**: lunch vouchers added monthly, kitchen restocked Tuesdays, parking closed for resurfacing, questions directed to #new‑hires, People team holds Thursday open office hours.

- **Level 2 difficulty spike** – 13/18 testers found the lamp‑keeper boss unfair; the second phase starts without a visible telegraph, causing an average of 6.4 attempts and three quits.  
- **Jump buffer too short on gamepad** – 11 testers complained; keyboard players had no issue.  
- **Camera clipping in narrow corridors** – 7 testers reported wall clipping; two experienced mild motion sickness during the rooftop chase.  
- **Performance drop on low‑spec hardware** – Frame rate fell to ~40 FPS on a GTX 1050 in the market scene.  
- **Unreliable crash on level 3 load** – One crash occurred during level 3 loading and has not yet been reproduced.

- **Move date & schedule**: Current office closes 27 Sep 18:00; employees work from home until 30 Sep; new office opens 1 Oct, but only 120 desks ready, so teams will rotate.  
- **Personal items**: Must fit into two company‑provided boxes by 25 Sep Wednesday; IT will move monitors/laptops—do not pack them yourself; unlabeled boxes will not be moved.  
- **Parking & transport**: Only 40 parking spots available; apply by 18 Sep to human.resources@example.com; company shuttle departs 08:15 from Levent.  
- **Cafeteria & amenities**: Located on 2nd floor of new building; lunch only for first two weeks; coffee machines not yet installed.  
- **Miscellaneous**: Company will move office plants and shared art; personal plants must be taken home by 25 Sep; employee cards remain unchanged; a brief briefing on move day will be held 24 Sep.
